[03:45:00 PM] Marcos Avila: I’m sorry to hear that’s happening! It’s definitely frustrating when the code arrives and immediately says it's expired.

1. Time Synchronization Issue (Most Common)
If your phone or computer’s internal clock is even 1–2 minutes off from the actual time, the system will think a brand-new code is already "expired."

The Fix: Go to your device settings and ensure "Set time and date automatically" is turned ON.

2. Signal Delays & Multiple Requests
If you’ve hit "Resend" several times, the codes might be arriving out of order. If you enter a code from an earlier text after a newer one has already been generated, the system will reject the old one as expired.

The Fix: Wait at least 15 minutes without requesting a new code to let the system reset. Then, request only one more and wait for it to arrive.

3. VPN or Proxy Interference
Sometimes a VPN can cause a mismatch between your device's location/time and our security servers, leading to instant expiration of security tokens.

The Fix: Fully disable any VPN or proxy on your device and try the verification again using your standard mobile data or home Wi-Fi.

If you are physically in Texas but getting a location error, it usually means the system is having trouble pinpointing your exact coordinates. Here is how we can fix that:

1. Check for a VPN or Proxy
This is the most common cause. If you have a VPN active (even if it's set to a Texas server), our system will automatically block the connection to comply with state regulations.

The Fix: Fully disable any VPN or proxy software and refresh your browser.

2. Enable Location Services
Your browser or device might be blocking the site from seeing your location.

On Mobile: Go to your phone Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → Make sure they are ON for your browser (Chrome/Safari).

On Desktop: Click the padlock icon in the address bar next to the URL → Site Settings → Location → Set to Allow.

3. Connection Routing
Sometimes your Internet Service Provider (ISP) might route your connection through a data center in a restricted state (like Louisiana or New Mexico).

The Fix: Try switching from Wi-Fi to mobile data (or vice versa) to see if a different connection clears the error.

4. Hard Refresh
If you were recently traveling or using a VPN, your browser might still be "remembering" that restricted location.

Windows: Ctrl + Shift + R

Mac: Cmd + Shift + R

Give those a try and let me know if you’re still blocked—I’m happy to dig deeper to get you back into your games!

[08:44:39 PM] Diana Lopez: Here is how you can check if a cancellation is possible:

Check the Dashboard: Look for a “Pending” status under the transaction or redemption history. Sometimes a “Cancel” button appears next to the request on the user end.

Contact Support Immediately: If no cancel button is present, the fastest way to stop the transaction is usually to contact customer support directly. Request them to void the request before it moves to the payout stage. Mention that you want to cancel it and convert the funds back to your playable balance (if applicable).

Understand the Cut-off Time: Many platforms allow cancellations only before the review team “locks” the transaction for processing. Once it moves to “Approved” or “Processing,” it likely cannot be stopped.

Re-purchase vs. Reversal: If the redemption cannot be cancelled, you might need to wait for the funds to arrive in your bank account and then use them to make a new purchase or deposit.

Final Recommendation: If you need to cancel a pending redemption, contact your platform’s customer service right away, as policies vary and timing is critical.

Browser settings → Autofill / Payment methods → disable autofill, then try again

[02:19:38 PM] Maritza Caceres: To set up your location, you basically need to tell your device and your browser that it's okay to share your coordinates with Jackpot Daily. Because we're a sweepstakes platform, our system has to be 100% sure you're in an eligible state before it lets you play.

Here is the quick guide to getting it "un-stuck":

📱 On Mobile (iPhone or Android)
Wi-Fi Check: Even if you aren't using Wi-Fi, turn it on. Your device uses nearby Wi-Fi signals to pin down your location much more accurately than GPS alone.

System Settings:

iPhone: Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services (On) > Safari/Chrome > Select "While Using the App" and toggle "Precise Location" to ON.

Android: Settings > Location > App Permissions > Browser > Select "Allow only while using the app" and toggle "Use precise location" to ON.

Refresh: Go back to the browser and refresh the page.

💻 On Desktop (Chrome, Safari, or Edge)
The "Lock" Icon: Look at the address bar at the top (where it says www.jackpotdaily.com). Click the padlock icon 🔒 on the left side of the URL.

Toggle Location: Find where it says "Location" and switch the toggle to "Allow".

Browser Settings: If that doesn't work, you might need to enable it in your computer's system settings:

Mac: Apple Menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services (ensure your browser is checked).

Windows: Start > Settings > Privacy & Security > Location > Ensure "Let apps access your location" is ON.

💡 Pro Tip for the "VPN Error"
If you've done all the above and it still says "VPN detected," try this:

Switch to Mobile Data: If you're on a laptop or Wi-Fi, try using your phone as a hotspot or just play on your phone's 5G. Sometimes home internet providers (ISPs) route your connection through a different state, which triggers our security "tripwire."

Give that a shot and let me know if the "VPN" message disappears!

[07:15:22 AM] Raul Figueroa: Hey! Welcome to Jackpot Daily support — I'm here to help! What can I do for you today?
[07:15:41 AM] t5592209566: Can you explain redemption rules. I have 100sc but 0 redemable
[07:17:10 AM] t5592209566: Ok
[07:17:29 AM] Raul Figueroa: Hey! Great question 

Having 100 SC doesn’t always mean they’re fully redeemable yet.

Before SC become redeemable, they usually need to be played through at least once (this is called a playthrough requirement). Until that’s completed, your redeemable balance can still show as 0.

Once you’ve used those SC in gameplay, they’ll convert into redeemable SC that you can cash out.
[07:18:25 AM] t5592209566: So if I won 100 dollars on a game. I have to play 100 to redeem 100
[07:19:09 AM] Raul Figueroa: It’s not exactly that you have to “play 100 to redeem 100,” but rather that the SC need to go through gameplay before becoming redeemable.

For example, if you win using SC, those winnings typically need to be played through at least once before they move into your redeemable balance.

So yes, in simple terms, they need to be used in gameplay first — but it doesn’t mean you lose them, just that they need to cycle through play.
[07:19:58 AM] t5592209566: Essentially meaning I have to win 200 to redeem 100 cause if I win 100 and then bad luck no wins gets down to 20 dollars I can't redeem
[07:20:54 AM] Raul Figueroa: You don’t need to win 200 to redeem 100 — it’s not doubling like that. The idea is just that your SC need to go through gameplay once before becoming redeemable.

However, you are right about one part: if your balance goes down while playing (for example from 100 to 20), then only what remains after playthrough would be available to redeem.

So it’s not about hitting a higher amount — it’s about completing the playthrough while maintaining your balance.

[02:55:06 AM] Eliezer Mejia: Thank you for reaching out! 

I’d be happy to clarify how the playthrough (wagering requirement) works on your account.

While it's true that you can enjoy almost any game on our platform while having an active bonus, not all games contribute the same percentage toward completing your playthrough requirements.

Slots: Generally contribute 100% toward your requirement. This means every $1 played counts as $1 toward clearing your bonus.

Table Games (like Baccarat or Roulette): Due to the different nature of these games, they often have a lower contribution rate (or 0%) toward the playthrough. This is why you may not see your progress bar move when playing Baccarat compared to playing Slots.

We recommend checking our Terms and Conditions or the specific rules of your active promotion to see the "Game Weighting" table. This will show you exactly which games will help you clear your bonus the fastest.

If you have any other questions about a specific game, feel free to ask!
[02:55:22 AM] t1058484489: Nope just wondering why the play thru doesn't work for baccarat
[02:56:19 AM] Eliezer Mejia: I understand your point. To be direct: Baccarat has a 0% contribution rate toward playthrough requirements.

While you are welcome to play Baccarat for fun or with your real money balance, any bets placed on this specific game do not count toward clearing a bonus. This is why you don't see your playthrough progress moving.

In contrast, Slots contribute 100%, which is why you see the requirement go down when playing them.

We recommend focusing your play on Slots if your goal is to complete the wagering requirements and redeem your bonus as quickly as possible.

Let us know if you have any other questions!

[02:19:38 PM] Maritza Caceres: To set up your location, you basically need to tell your device and your browser that it's okay to share your coordinates with Jackpot Daily. Because we're a sweepstakes platform, our system has to be 100% sure you're in an eligible state before it lets you play.

Here is the quick guide to getting it "un-stuck":

📱 On Mobile (iPhone or Android)
Wi-Fi Check: Even if you aren't using Wi-Fi, turn it on. Your device uses nearby Wi-Fi signals to pin down your location much more accurately than GPS alone.

System Settings:

iPhone: Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services (On) > Safari/Chrome > Select "While Using the App" and toggle "Precise Location" to ON.

Android: Settings > Location > App Permissions > Browser > Select "Allow only while using the app" and toggle "Use precise location" to ON.

Refresh: Go back to the browser and refresh the page.

💻 On Desktop (Chrome, Safari, or Edge)
The "Lock" Icon: Look at the address bar at the top (where it says www.jackpotdaily.com). Click the padlock icon 🔒 on the left side of the URL.

Toggle Location: Find where it says "Location" and switch the toggle to "Allow".

Browser Settings: If that doesn't work, you might need to enable it in your computer's system settings:

Mac: Apple Menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services (ensure your browser is checked).

Windows: Start > Settings > Privacy & Security > Location > Ensure "Let apps access your location" is ON.

💡 Pro Tip for the "VPN Error"
If you've done all the above and it still says "VPN detected," try this:

Switch to Mobile Data: If you're on a laptop or Wi-Fi, try using your phone as a hotspot or just play on your phone's 5G. Sometimes home internet providers (ISPs) route your connection through a different state, which triggers our security "tripwire."

Give that a shot and let me know if the "VPN" message disappears!

[03:45:00 PM] Marcos Avila: I’m sorry to hear that’s happening! It’s definitely frustrating when the code arrives and immediately says it's expired.

1. Time Synchronization Issue (Most Common)
If your phone or computer’s internal clock is even 1–2 minutes off from the actual time, the system will think a brand-new code is already "expired."

The Fix: Go to your device settings and ensure "Set time and date automatically" is turned ON.

2. Signal Delays & Multiple Requests
If you’ve hit "Resend" several times, the codes might be arriving out of order. If you enter a code from an earlier text after a newer one has already been generated, the system will reject the old one as expired.

The Fix: Wait at least 15 minutes without requesting a new code to let the system reset. Then, request only one more and wait for it to arrive.

3. VPN or Proxy Interference
Sometimes a VPN can cause a mismatch between your device's location/time and our security servers, leading to instant expiration of security tokens.

The Fix: Fully disable any VPN or proxy on your device and try the verification again using your standard mobile data or home Wi-Fi.

If you are physically in Texas but getting a location error, it usually means the system is having trouble pinpointing your exact coordinates. Here is how we can fix that:

1. Check for a VPN or Proxy
This is the most common cause. If you have a VPN active (even if it's set to a Texas server), our system will automatically block the connection to comply with state regulations.

The Fix: Fully disable any VPN or proxy software and refresh your browser.

2. Enable Location Services
Your browser or device might be blocking the site from seeing your location.

On Mobile: Go to your phone Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → Make sure they are ON for your browser (Chrome/Safari).

On Desktop: Click the padlock icon in the address bar next to the URL → Site Settings → Location → Set to Allow.

3. Connection Routing
Sometimes your Internet Service Provider (ISP) might route your connection through a data center in a restricted state (like Louisiana or New Mexico).

The Fix: Try switching from Wi-Fi to mobile data (or vice versa) to see if a different connection clears the error.

4. Hard Refresh
If you were recently traveling or using a VPN, your browser might still be "remembering" that restricted location.

Windows: Ctrl + Shift + R

Mac: Cmd + Shift + R

Give those a try and let me know if you’re still blocked—I’m happy to dig deeper to get you back into your games!

[06:07:39 AM] Karen Perez: Hey! I get why that’s frustrating — especially if you’ve got a balance sitting there.

If your account is currently under a self-exclusion or marked as disabled, that will block access to features like redemption. While the restriction is in place, you won’t be able to log in or submit a cashout request.

Outside of that, redemptions also need a couple of standard requirements:

Minimum of 100 Sweepstakes Coins
Those coins must be played through at least once
Account needs to be fully verified

In your case though, it sounds like the account status (self-exclusion/disabled) is the main blocker.

You’re right: if a full self-exclusion were active, you wouldn’t be able to log in or make a deposit at all. So if you’re able to do both, then it likely isn’t a full self-exclusion causing the issue.

That means the redemption block is probably coming from something else, most commonly:

Account not fully verified (KYC still pending or incomplete)
Not meeting the minimum 100 SC requirement
SC hasn’t completed the 1x playthrough
A temporary restriction or review on the account

Since you mentioned the account is very new, verification is the most likely reason here.

That said, having 100+ SC is only one part of the requirement. For a redemption to go through, all of the following need to be met:

Minimum 100 SC
1x playthrough completed on those SC
Full account verification (KYC approved)

With a new account, the most common blockers are:

The SC hasn’t been fully played through yet
Verification hasn’t been completed or approved

Verification Not Approved — The most common reasons are blurry photos, mismatched info (name or DOB), or expired documents. You should have received an email with the specific reason if it was declined.

Partial Verification — You might have verified your email and phone, but the system still needs your government-issued ID and selfie through Socure.

Sync Issue — Sometimes your browser just needs a nudge to show your updated status. Try logging out and back in, or do a quick hard refresh (Ctrl + Shift + R).

Quick things to check for your ID submission:

Must be government-issued and not expired

All 4 corners must be visible

Front and back required (JPEG or PNG only)

No screenshots from a PC or phone

Re-purchase vs. Reversal: If the redemption cannot be cancelled, you might need to wait for the funds to arrive in your bank account and then use them to make a new purchase or deposit.
